problem_statement: Elevate the TailAdmin ecommerce console into a coherent revenue operations workspace by introducing a shared Revenue Ops Rail that rides above the page content across the operator's key admin routes. The rail is a compact, on-brand status band carrying four revenue/pipeline/fulfillment tiles, a scope toggle, and a live scope readout. It must render inside the existing admin layout shell on the ecommerce home, the profile console, and the calendar console so the revenue pulse follows the operator, must recolor and lay out in the native TailAdmin light/dark language, must stay overflow-free on mobile, and its scope toggle must keep the terminal readout in sync with the active scope.
required_content: A shared Revenue Ops Rail component renders inside the existing (admin) layout on the ecommerce home, the profile page, and the calendar page, so the same rail appears across multiple admin routes rather than on a single page.
The rail shows a titled band ('Revenue Ops Rail') with four operational tiles: Revenue attainment, Pipeline coverage, At-risk orders, and Fulfillment SLA, each with a value and a short helper note.

The rail adopts the TailAdmin visual system (rounded cards, gray borders, white/dark translucent surfaces, brand-blue accents, muted helper text) and does not introduce an off-brand dark slate or neon palette.
The rail's tile row stays inside the viewport on mobile without causing horizontal page overflow; tiles wrap or shrink rather than forcing the document wider than the screen.

The rail's scope toggle button flips between Global and Regional coverage and the adjacent scope readout re-syncs to the active scope ('Scope: Global coverage' / 'Scope: Regional coverage') after each toggle.
Existing EcommerceMetrics, Monthly Sales, Statistics, Customers Demographic, sidebar, header, dark-mode styling, and the profile/calendar page bodies remain visually stable.
design_constraints: Render the rail through the shared (admin) layout so it appears consistently across the whitelisted admin routes; do not paste a separate copy per page or hang it off a standalone marketing route.
Keep the rail in TailAdmin's restrained admin language: rounded-2xl surfaces, gray borders, white/dark translucent backgrounds, brand-blue accents, small muted helper text.
Do not introduce a new global palette (no off-brand dark slate / neon recolor of the rail) or an external icon/chart library beyond the repo's existing setup.
The four-tile row must remain scannable and must not overflow the page horizontally on mobile; use fluid/wrapping tiles rather than fixed wide non-wrapping cells.
The scope toggle must update both the active button state and the terminal scope readout together; the readout must not freeze on its initial value after interaction.
state_constraints: The shared Revenue Ops Rail must render on the ecommerce home, profile, and calendar routes and be captured as the main before/after evidence.
The rail's mobile tile row must be captured to confirm no horizontal page overflow.
The scope-toggle interaction state must be captured after clicking the toggle to confirm the readout re-syncs.
Profile, calendar, and blank pages are regression anchors and must not be restyled off-brand to satisfy the task.
All rail content must be inspectable as React/Next DOM, not flattened into screenshots or hidden offscreen.

change_completion: A shared Revenue Ops Rail is added through the (admin) layout and appears on the ecommerce home, profile, and calendar routes.
The rail carries the four operational tiles (Revenue attainment, Pipeline coverage, At-risk orders, Fulfillment SLA) with values, helper notes, a scope toggle, and a scope readout.
The scope toggle re-syncs the terminal readout to the active scope after interaction.
design_consistency: The rail uses TailAdmin card, border, typography, accent, and spacing conventions and stays subordinate to the dashboard hierarchy.
The rail keeps the native light/dark palette and does not recolor into an off-brand dark slate or neon band.
The rail reads as a refined admin workflow rather than a pasted marketing/analytics section.
regression: EcommerceMetrics, Monthly Sales, Statistics, Customers Demographic, sidebar, header, profile, and calendar bodies remain reachable and visually stable.
Existing dark-mode classes and responsive shell behavior are not broken by the rail.
responsive: Desktop lays the four rail tiles in a balanced band above the page content.
Mobile wraps or shrinks the tiles cleanly and avoids horizontal page overflow or text clipping.

author_notes: Repo-grounded TailAdmin Next.js dashboard restyle. The shared Revenue Ops Rail is rendered through the existing (admin) layout across the ecommerce, profile, and calendar routes, reusing TailAdmin's rounded-card, brand-blue, muted-helper design language and the repo's local product/user/country image assets. This task tests whether an agent can extend an existing admin workflow with a consistent cross-page status rail in the native visual system, keep it responsive and overflow-free, and wire the scope toggle so the readout stays in sync, rather than appending an off-brand section or leaving a stale terminal state.
